Question: A college student drove his compact car \(120\) miles home for the weekend and averaged \(30\) miles per gallon. On the return trip the student drove his parents’ SUV and averaged only \(20\) miles per gallon. What was the average gas mileage, in miles per gallon, for the round trip?
Solution:
Round-trip miles per gallon means total miles divided by total gallons, so first find the fuel used on each leg. The compact car uses
\[
\frac{120}{30}=4\text{ gallons},
\]
and the SUV uses
\[
\frac{120}{20}=6\text{ gallons}.
\]
The total distance is \(120+120=240\) miles, and the total fuel consumption is \(4+6=10\) gallons. Thus the round-trip gas mileage is
\[
\frac{240}{10}=\boxed{24}
\]
miles per gallon, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
